newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs rise at close, pork bellies end weak.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs rise at close, pork bellies end weak.

text.p: CME February hog futures shot up in the closing range on stop-close-only buy orders and other months ended mixed while pork bellies were lower on pressure from weakness in cash product, traders said.
Hogs closed up 0.750 cent to off 0.075 with February up most at 77.500 cents. Pork bellies ended with losses of 1.450 to 0.450 cents with February off 0.525 at 77.425 cents.

Higher cash hogs added to expectations of a bullish quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report and futures trended higher with buying by Cargill Investor Services in February at the close touching off buy stops, traders said.

The report is expected to show lighter than year ago U.S. hog supplies. Analysts estimates for All hogs as of December 1 averaged 98.4 percent of a year ago in a range of 95 to 101 percent. Hogs kept for breeding estimates averaged 101.6 in a range of 99.9 to 104 and kept for market estimates averaged 97.5 in a range of 94 to 99 percent.
Cash hog markets showed strength as packers planned to increase the kill rate over the weekend to make up for the holiday on Wednesday.
The latest lean hog index was off $0.76 at $75.44 per cwt.
Rand Financials, LIT division of First Options, LFG and Lind-Waldock bought early while R.J. O'Brien sold. Rand spread long July/short April, pit sources said.
In hog options, R.J. O'Brien did risk reversals in June, buying 70 and 72 puts an selling 80 calls. Commission house bought February 75 puts an 76 calls, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures continued to show pressure from a weak tone to cash bellies. USDA reported cash bellies $2 per cwt lower at noon as expected which kept futures under previous levels. Pressure continued late to press prices to new days lows by the close, traders said.
Cash bellies were under pressure from high prices and slow retail demand during the holidays. This offset support at times from low storage stocks, they said.
